subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose browser network traffic to the model, and should the first API be passive-only or include active request interception/mutation?
rationale: The implementation shape affects authenticated browser traffic exposure, model-visible sensitive data, and profile-specific browser security guarantees, so automation should not choose the permanent API boundary alone.

options.title: Guarded passive-first API
options.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body capture through a model-facing browser plugin action with redaction, permissions, and profile limits, while deferring active mutation.

options.title: Full interception API
options.body: Approve a broader enable/list/intercept API that includes active interception or mutation, with an explicit security design and tests for each supported profile mode.

options.title: Keep operator-only for now
options.body: Leave requests and responsebody as CLI/control-server debugging routes until maintainers are ready to expose network data to agents.

recommendation.title: Guarded passive-first API
recommendation.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body capture through a model-facing browser plugin action with redaction, permissions, and profile limits, while deferring active mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current schema, dispatcher, docs, and bundled browser-plugin ownership history point most strongly to this owner for the API/security decision.
